subject: Chemistry
title: Lavoisier Names Oxygen
description: A quick win: understand Lavoisier Names Oxygen.

hook.text: Antoine Lavoisier didn't discover oxygen, but he figured out what it actually does—and named it.

buildup.text: Joseph Priestley isolated the gas in 1774. He called it 'dephlogisticated air.' Nobody understood it.

discovery.text: Lavoisier proved this gas was essential for burning and breathing. He named it oxygen: 'acid-maker.'

twist.text: The name was actually wrong. Oxygen doesn't make acids—hydrogen does. But the name stuck.

climax.text: Lavoisier's work killed the phlogiston theory and created modern chemistry's first element list.

punchline.text: Named it wrong, understood it right. Chemistry was born.

quiz.question: What did Lavoisier prove about oxygen?
options: It is essential for combustion and respiration

details.summary: Antoine Lavoisier named oxygen from the Greek for acid-former in 1778, believing incorrectly that all acids contained it. More importantly, he demonstrated oxygen's central role in combustion.
details.whyItMatters: Lavoisier's oxygen work overthrew the phlogiston theory that had dominated chemistry for a century and established the principle of systematic chemical nomenclature that scientists still follow.
takeaways: Lavoisier named oxygen from Greek roots meaning acid-former
He proved combustion is combination with oxygen, not release of phlogiston
His systematic naming convention replaced confusing alchemical terminology

faq.question: Why was Lavoisier's naming of oxygen actually based on a mistake?
faq.answer: Lavoisier believed oxygen was a component of all acids, so he named it acid-former from the Greek oxys and genes. This is incorrect because many acids like hydrochloric acid contain no oxygen, and many oxygen-containing compounds are not acids. The incorrect name stuck despite the error.

faq.question: How did Lavoisier disprove phlogiston theory using oxygen?
faq.answer: Lavoisier carefully weighed metals before and after burning, showing they gained mass rather than losing phlogiston. He demonstrated that the mass gain exactly matched the oxygen consumed from sealed air..
